title: G6 Battery Reporting
body:
Hi,

Been using `xDrip` for a long time, just transitioned to the G6 without any problems, except for during the warm-up phase I received a `Critical Low Battery` error and now am seeing this voltage/resistance reading:

![dex](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5959454/47027843-37d5d580-d136-11e8-8c08-b9d533daeaae.png)

I am receiving a replacement sensor, just wondering if there were any reports of this happening upon activating a new G6 sensor. I hadn't used the official G6 app to activate.

I'm on a Pixel 2 with the latest Android 9 security patch.

comments.body:
My experience with the new g6 batteries is in line with what you see in terms of the voltage and resistance numbers.  Others have seen similar values as well.  

Regarding the error... if you go into your settings at modify the "low battery" number from whatever the default is to something lower... I set mine to 260 some time ago for the g5 and it may have to come down to a new number as I learn more about how these g6 batteries behave.  The setting is in the g5/g6 debug settings area at the bottom, "Adjust battery warning level".

Thanks for the response @gitanO0! I've modified those values -- have your transmitters lasted as long? I assume we just need to edit some of the battery alerting features to account for the different battery characteristics of the G6? Unless the G6 I received is just faulty.

The battery metrics for G6 are different. xDrip does normally automatically adjust for what we know about G6 so far. What would be helpful would be to build up some information about what a fresh battery level looks like and what it is at 90-100 days and what it is when the transmitter stops functioning correctly. Feel free to add such information to this issue..

Transmitter day 81, sensor inserted today
Voltage A 309
Voltage B 288
Resistance 9296 
The range of resistance numbers is too big to make any sense to me. Been reading with both Dex receiver and xDrip+ on a Pixel 3a, and can't tell if I'll even make the guaranteed 90 days (it might be good if I didn't and got a warranty-replacement transmitter).
How long should I expect this to last?
Related to #1085.

The resistance value reported for G6 transmitters whose serial number did not start with 80 or 81 was never correct.  Neither was the temperature.  The format Dexcom used to communicate was changed.  There is a pull request to correct xDrip to read the new format correctly.  In the meantime, both resistance and temperature have been removed from the recent releases of xDrip.  Hopefully, the pull request will be approved soon.

Voltage B is the best parameter to look at to judge how long your transmitter is going to last.  However, what is important is the trend rather than the absolute value.
If the voltage is on a downward trend, you will know that the battery will die soon and you may need to take action.

Please look at the following two figures.  They show Voltage B for two different transmitters (neither 80XXXX or 81XXXX).  Neither reached a downward trend before day 110.  
But, please note the difference in the absolute values.  
The voltage is measured by the chip itself.  So, the reference for the measurement varies from part to part.  Therefore, the accuracy is not perfect and you shouldn't compare the absolute values.

![Screenshot 2021-03-01 175428](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51497406/109570343-e1278700-7ab7-11eb-9ac3-0e88611a5415.png)
![Screenshot 2021-03-01 175449](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51497406/109570357-e5ec3b00-7ab7-11eb-8b57-d2c6f91790ef.png)

As this issue is neither related to an xDrip bug nor a feature request, I am going to close the issue.  Please use the support channels to consult with the user community including the developers.
https://www.facebook.com/groups/xDripG5
https://gitter.im/jamorham/xDrip-plus

You can continue to add comments.  If you feel this should not be closed, please post and let us talk about it.  We can always reopen if needed.  However, issues should only be used for reporting an xDrip bug for requesting a new feature, which has no existing work-around.
